title: Data Centers and Large Loads in Power Systems: A Comprehensive Review of Modeling, Applications, and Industry Practices
content: The rapid growth of large electricity-consuming facilities, including hyperscale data centers, hydrogen electrolyzers, cryptocurrency mining operations, electric vehicle charging hubs, and electrified industrial processes, is introducing new challenges for transmission planning and power system reliability. Unlike traditional aggregated loads, many emerging large loads are highly concentrated, exhibit rapid power variations, and increasingly rely on power-electronic interfaces, resulting in dynamic behaviors that are not adequately represented by conventional load models. Consequently, accurate load modeling has become essential for steady-state analysis, stability assessment, interconnection studies, and long-term transmission planning. This paper presents a comprehensive review of large load modeling methodologies and their applications in future transmission planning. The evolution of load modeling is examined from classical static ZIP models and induction motor representations to composite load models and emerging power-electronic load models such as LDEV1 and PERC1. Measurement-based and component-based modeling approaches are reviewed along with their advantages, limitations, and validation requirements. The paper further discusses the role of large load models in power flow studies, voltage and transient stability assessments, electromagnetic transient simulations, and planning under uncertainty. Current utility practices, industry initiatives, and evolving interconnection requirements are also summarized. Finally, key challenges are identified, including model validation, data availability, platform inconsistencies, and the representation of converter-dominated loads. The review highlights the need for standardized modeling frameworks, improved measurement-based validation, and enhanced collaboration among utilities, researchers, and regulators to support the reliable integration of large loads into future power systems.
